verdict.rationale: ClickUp documents an official MCP server that lets AI agents work with workspace data such as tasks, lists, folders and docs "using natural language," with action tools like time tracking and report building. In-product, Brain² answers natural-language questions and Super Agent claims to "delegate any task." However, the evidence for operating the product broadly through natural-language commands is thin: Brain² is shown mainly answering questions, and the action path largely depends on an external AI client through MCP. missing for 10: documented in-app natural-language command execution across core features (creating and editing tasks, views and automations via Brain²), detail on what Super Agent can actually do, independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language operation works reliably.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: lets external AI agents interact with ClickUp Workspace data—like tasks, lists, folders, and docs—using natural language
